title: Bollywood Rallies Behind Sonam Wangchuk as Hunger Strike Over NEET Crisis Enters Fourth Week
excerpt: From Hrithik Roshan to Sonakshi Sinha, a growing wave of film industry voices is demanding the government engage with the climate activist, who was forcibly hospitalized on day 21 of his fast.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Hrithik Roshan publicly supports Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike, marking a shift in Bollywood's response.
  • Sonakshi Sinha's emotional video plea highlights the urgency of Wangchuk's protest against NEET exam irregularities.
  • Wangchuk was forcibly hospitalized on July 18 after deteriorating health during his 21-day hunger strike.
  • Growing celebrity support is increasing pressure on the government to address the NEET crisis.
  • Hrithik Roshan became the highest-profile Bollywood A-lister to back Sonam Wangchuk's indefinite hunger strike, sharing a protest video on Instagram and referencing his role in Super 30.
  • Sonakshi Sinha posted an emotional video asking "Koi sunn kyun nahi raha?" as Wangchuk's fast against NEET exam irregularities entered its 21st day at Jantar Mantar.
  • Police forcibly shifted Wangchuk to Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital on July 18 on Delhi High Court directions after doctors warned his condition had deteriorated.
  • The growing celebrity support — spanning Zeenat Aman, Anurag Kashyap, Swara Bhasker, and Naseeruddin Shah — has amplified pressure on the government to engage with protesters.

Bollywood actor Hrithik Roshan on Friday became the first major A-list star to publicly back climate activist Sonam Wangchuk, who has been on an indefinite hunger strike at Delhi's Jantar Mantar since June 28, demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged irregularities in the NEET-UG examination.

Roshan reposted a video of Wangchuk on his Instagram Stories — originally shared by actress Lisa Ray — in which the activist questioned why so many people have stayed silent while students suffer the consequences of alleged exam paper leaks. "This sounds true," Roshan wrote alongside the clip. "I learnt about the trauma students go through when I played a teacher in one of my movies," he added, referencing his portrayal of mathematician Anand Kumar in Super 30.

A Cascade of Celebrity Voices

Roshan's intervention drew mixed reactions but marked a turning point in what had been a cautious response from Bollywood's biggest names. Before him, actress Sonakshi Sinha had posted an emotional Instagram video that went viral, pleading with the public: "Koi sunn kyun nahi raha? Nobody cares." The video drew millions of views and renewed attention to Wangchuk's deteriorating health.

Filmmaker Kiran Rao, the former wife of actor Aamir Khan, posted a detailed statement of solidarity. "I stand in solidarity with Sonam Wangchuk, Abhijit Deepke, the CJP, and all the citizens of this country who are protesting for the rights of our students," she wrote. "It is so distressing to witness the complete silence that this hunger strike has been met with even after 19 days."

"It is so distressing to witness the complete silence that this hunger strike has been met with even after 19 days. What will it take for those in power to listen to the people?"

— Kiran Rao, filmmaker

Aamir Khan, whose 2009 hit 3 Idiots featured a character widely believed to be inspired by Wangchuk, addressed the situation publicly, clarifying that reports of Wangchuk's grave illness were exaggerated. Omi Vaidya, who played the character Chhatur in the film, also shared a video urging people not to turn their backs on the activist.

The list of supporters has continued to grow. Veteran actress Zeenat Aman issued an emotional appeal on social media, prompting Bigg Boss 14 winner Rubina Dilaik to share the post with the message: "He is a real hero, don't let him die fighting for our country's own good." Actress Swara Bhasker went further, physically visiting the protest site at Jantar Mantar and later calling out the broader film industry for its silence. "Many fear backlash for defending him," she said.

Others who have spoken out include directors Anurag Kashyap and Zoya Akhtar, actors Naseeruddin Shah, Shabana Azmi, Ratna Pathak Shah, Abhay Deol, Soni Razdan, Prakash Raj, Parvathy Thiruvothu, Lisa Ray, and comedian Vir Das. Author Arundhati Roy also publicly backed the protest.

Forcible Hospitalization Sparks Outrage

The growing celebrity support coincided with a dramatic escalation on July 18, when Delhi Police shifted Wangchuk from Jantar Mantar to Safdarjung Hospital against his wishes. The move followed directions from the Delhi High Court, which had observed that "the life of any citizen is precious" and ordered daily medical assessments of the fasting activist.

Television footage showed dozens of security personnel holding large white cloth sheets as a makeshift curtain before Wangchuk was taken away. Protesters accused police of using excessive force, with Cockroach Janta Party leader Abhijeet Deepke alleging officers "abused Sonam sir and dragged him away."

Safdarjung Hospital said Wangchuk was weak from prolonged fasting and dehydration but stable. He refused intravenous fluids and oral medication, the hospital confirmed. His wife, Gitanjali J. Angmo, demanded that no treatment be administered without the family's consent and sought his transfer to a private facility. On Sunday, the Delhi High Court declined to order his discharge, ruling the government's decision was not arbitrary.

What's at Stake

Wangchuk, 59, launched his fast in solidarity with the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party, which formed after alleged NEET-UG paper leaks in May affected millions of aspiring medical students. The protesters are demanding Pradhan's resignation, greater accountability for examination failures, and systemic reforms to India's competitive testing infrastructure.

The NEET controversy hits close to home for lakhs of Indian families, including those in the diaspora who invest years of preparation and significant financial resources in competitive exam coaching. Wangchuk himself is a globally recognized figure — his innovative work in education in Ladakh, including the development of ice stupas, earned him the Ramon Magsaysay Award and made him a household name as the real-life inspiration for 3 Idiots.

As his hunger strike stretches into its fourth week, the central question remains whether the government will open a dialogue with Wangchuk and the protesters — or continue to let the standoff escalate.
